newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom head sees stable 97 revenues.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom head sees stable 97 revenues.

text.p: France Telecom Chairman Michel Bon said on Thursday he expected 1997 turnover to be similar to this year's as increased subscriptions would offset the tariff cuts the operator would make in the face of increased competition.

Bon said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television he did not expect a significant impact from lower tariffs, as a rise in subscriber rates would compensate for reductions in prices for long-distance calls.
France Telecom expects to lose market share after deregulation, which would usher in competition from world-scale operators from Europe, such as British Telecom, the United States, and Asia, he said.
But the state-owned operator expects growth in volumes to compensate for the loss in market share, he said.
France Telecom will "rebalance" tariffs until 1998, when the market will be fully open to competition, and its tariffs will then be equivalent to those of British Telecom, he said.
Bon said on Monday that France Telecom would be ready to go to the stockmarket in the middle of April 1997, through a public offering.

Even taking the lower end valuation of France Telecom at 100 billion francs, the market would not be able to absorb 49 percent of the capital in one offering, so a second tranche was likely. The higher valuation was 200 billion francs.
France Telecom made a net attributable profit of 9.2 billion francs in 1995, on turnover of 147.8 billion.
